subject: Urgent: Checkoutly capacity corridor exceeded — proposed mitigations & customer comms
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@checkoutly.com>, ops-lead@checkoutly.com
Date: 2026-10-08T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Throughput corridor breach — Checkoutly prod

Team — monitoring tripped on Checkoutly's production fleet at ~14:05 PDT. Immediate story: p99 token latency jumped from ~220ms to 1.6s for Gen API streaming endpoints; overall token throughput dropped ~28% as QPS throttles kicked in. Attached is the short metrics snapshot (spike-metrics-graph.png).

What we have so far:
- Spike started 14:02, peaked 14:07, ongoing at degraded state (still elevated at 14:10).
- Autoscale didn't fully absorb burst; per-customer reserved pool hit configured 'corridor' limit and we began shedding to the shared pool which led to queueing and throttle spikes.
- KV cache hit-rates dropped for the 175B model variant used by Checkoutly (likely due to sequence-length change).

Immediate asks (I can act on 1–2 once we decide):
1) SRE: can we temporarily raise Checkoutly's corridor cap to allow burst to finish into their reserved pool? This is a config flip; expected <10m to take effect but requires coordination with routing.
2) Eng/Product: would a short-lived fallback to the 70B variant (same family) be acceptable for 10–15m to reduce tail latency while we stabilize? Tradeoff: slight quality delta but large latency improvement.
3) Customer comms: Marissa / Ben — need a short note to Aisha and ops team acknowledging the incident and immediate mitigations.

Attachments: spike-metrics-graph.png (png, 78KB)

Jonas
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@checkoutly.com>, ops-lead@checkoutly.com
Date: 2026-10-08T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Throughput corridor breach — Checkoutly prod

On 2026-10-08 14:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Team — monitoring tripped on Checkoutly's production fleet at ~14:05 PDT.

Confirmed — I'm looking at tracer dumps and router telemetry. Quick findings and recommended steps: 

Findings:
- Routing scoreboard shows Checkoutly hit corridor_max concurrent tokens at 14:04:58; traffic overflow to shared pool began at 14:05:02.
- CPU saturation (decoder kernels) observed on two pods in the dedicated pool; those pods are prioritizing streaming and backpressure is cascading to the queue.
- KV cache TTLs for the session keyspace dropped due to a sudden increase in unique prefixes (likely a UX change on Checkoutly's side).

Immediate mitigations (15–30m):
A) Raise corridor cap by +40% for Checkoutly (config flip) — low risk; will require routing restart for the affected pool (we can do a rolling restart to avoid a full outage). Expected effect: reduces overflow and rebalances to dedicated GPUs.
B) Enable ephemeral burst pool (if allowed by tenant config) — combined with A) should relieve queue.
C) Short fallback to 70B variant for new sessions only (no migration) — requires product sign-off; I can gate at the routing layer.

Product asks (for roadmap / postmortem):
- Need an opt-in 'soft corridor' mode that auto-buys short bursts for high-value tenants for up to 15m before invoking shared fallback. This is a product + billing + runtime change (medium-term).
- Investigate model selector heuristics: prefer fallbacks that preserve generation semantics for streaming clients.

I'll start action A and B now (pending Marissa's go-ahead and confirmation we send the customer note). Rolling restart ETA for affected replicas: ~10 minutes from approval.

Ben
SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@checkoutly.com>, ops-lead@checkoutly.com

Date: 2026-10-08T14:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Throughput corridor breach — Checkoutly prod

Aisha — quick note to confirm we're actively working this. Proposed customer-facing message below; please let me know if you'd like edits before we send. Ben/Jonas: please proceed with the corridor cap increase + ephemeral burst pool once I have Aisha's go-ahead; Ben, please include the fallback-to-70B option in the comms as "temporary quality tradeoff" if we need to take it.

Proposed message to Checkoutly users (short):
---
Subject: Brief service impact on Redwood inference for Checkoutly (Oct 8, 14:00 PDT)

Hi Aisha / Checkoutly ops team —

We observed an elevated latency and reduced throughput on Checkoutly's inference endpoint beginning ~14:02 PDT. Our engineering team has applied temporary mitigation steps to restore normal traffic routing and reduce latency; you may see a short period where model responses either (a) have slightly different performance characteristics or (b) fall back to a slightly smaller model for a brief window while we stabilize.

We do not expect customer data exposure. We will follow up with a post-incident report within 48 hours detailing root cause and next steps, and we will schedule a joint review if helpful.

If you have immediate concerns, reply to this thread or ping your Redwood account lead.
---

Customer ask: can you confirm you'd like us to send the message above now? Also, is Checkoutly open to the temporary fallback to the 70B variant if it speeds recovery? (We will only do that with your explicit sign-off.)

Marissa
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

A couple of asks from our side: 
- We'll expect a post-incident report within 48 hours with root cause, mitigation timeline and whether any SLA credits will be applied.
- Procurement copied here for visibility on any billing impact from burst usage.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Aisha
